steps.title: Your first program is a scoreboard
steps.body:
Every placement test starts the same way: read some numbers, work something out, **print** the answer. To do that, a program needs somewhere to keep values while it works. Those places are **variables**.

In five minutes you’ll read a tiny program, predict what it prints, watch its variables change, and fix one yourself.

options.why: Right. score was 10, then became 15, and + stitched the text together.
Here + adds 10 and 5 as numbers first (line 4 has no text in it), giving 15.
Without quotes, name and score mean the variables, so their VALUES are printed.
score = score + 5 changed the box to 15 before the println ran.

steps.title: Variables, types and println
points: A **variable** is a named box with a **type**: `int` whole numbers, `double` decimals, `boolean` true/false, `char` one character, `String` text.
`=` means **store**, not "equals". `score = score + 5` reads the old value, adds 5, and saves the result.
`System.out.println(x)` prints x and moves to a new line. `print` stays on the same line.

steps.prompt: A classic trap. What does this print?

options.why: Mixing text and numbers with + is allowed; Java turns the numbers into text.
Java works left to right: "Sum: " + 5 is the text "Sum: 5", and then + 3 joins another 3. Brackets fix it: "Sum: " + (a + b).
a and b are outside the quotes, so their values (5 and 3) are used.
Yes! Once text is on the left, every + joins text. Write "Sum: " + (a + b) to add first.

steps.prompt: Your turn. Fix the trap so it prints the real total, "Sum: 8". We'll also try your line with other numbers in a and b.
steps.hint: Brackets are worked out first, so put the addition in brackets.
steps.explain: `(a + b)` is added as numbers **before** it meets the text, so you get `Sum: 8` instead of `Sum: 53`.
